### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **21** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/cli/src/utils/database-driver-flag.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**18** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json eb9ef791bdc0034559924924bfffd3f762b531d6`.

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/cli/src/utils/database-driver-flag.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `os dev (command, 32 pages)`, `os serve (command, 30 pages)`
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **148** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json eb9ef791bdc0034559924924bfffd3f762b531d6` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `5bf5a5550351bc49be3c944f5220f6cc1e116bb4` — the merge of head `b0b835ba75c9bb42ba7299874859065c9f3ef68f` into base `eb9ef791bdc0034559924924bfffd3f762b531d6`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 5bf5a5550351bc49be3c944f5220f6cc1e116bb4 && git checkout 5bf5a5550351bc49be3c944f5220f6cc1e116bb4
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin eb9ef791bdc0034559924924bfffd3f762b531d6 b0b835ba75c9bb42ba7299874859065c9f3ef68f && git checkout -B drift-repro eb9ef791bdc0034559924924bfffd3f762b531d6 && git merge --no-ff b0b835ba75c9bb42ba7299874859065c9f3ef68f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json eb9ef791bdc0034559924924bfffd3f762b531d6
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs eb9ef791bdc0034559924924bfffd3f762b531d6` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `b0b835ba75c9bb42ba7299874859065c9f3ef68f`
Local-runs: none

Read: card #21492 (body and every comment, triage's first grade `5963328372`, its lane amendment `5963850458`, the reversal to retire `5964828718`, the A-on-both-hosts ruling `5967968291`, and the one-landing restaging `5969357294`), card #21572 (body and every comment, including triage's `5969348039`), PR #21598's body and 31-file list, the net diff against `main` at this head (merge base `901e7cf13a`), and the check-runs on this head. Nothing was built, run or re-run locally.

### ① Derived judgments

Governing text: triage `5967968291` (A: retire at the declaration on both hosts; Q2 a: `os migrate` and a programmatic `createStandaloneStack` refuse the schemes too; `driver-memory` not retired; a direct construction is not a boot spelling), restaged by `5969348039` / `5969357294` as one landing carrying #21572's row commit `d480ef0d70`.

**Spec (`packages/spec/src/data/driver/config-registry.zod.ts`, the #21572 row) — right.**
- The `memory` row moves `memory`, `mingo`, `in-memory` from `aliases` to `contractOnlyAliases` beside `inmemory`; every other row is byte-unchanged. `DRIVER_ID_ALIASES` is built from both faces, so `resolveDriverId` still answers `memory` for all four spellings and `DatasourceSchema` still parses `driver: memory` (pinned in `config-registry.test.ts`). The selection face narrows by derivation: `DATABASE_DRIVER_SELECTION_ALIASES` 17 to 14 entries, `DATABASE_DRIVER_SELECTION_IDS` 7 to 6, `resolveDatabaseDriverId` answers `undefined` for the four. ⛔ No consumer-side subtraction anywhere in the diff, which is the card's and the design notes' term.
- Public surface: no export added, removed or retyped (`readonly string[]` / `readonly BuiltinDriverId[]` kept; `BuiltinDriverId` still carries `memory`). Only VALUES move, which is why no `api-surface` or `authorable-surface` shard moves (`TypeScript Type Check` green; the dev's `check:generated` reading agrees). The stale doc comments the #21572 report flagged (the `aliases` TSDoc, the "nothing withheld today" paragraph, the seventeen-entries count, `hasLocalDefault`) are all rewritten.
- The spec pins the row owes (#21572 "Pins"): three spellings not selection ids, all four contract-only and parsing, other rows unchanged — all three present and the third one asserts the whole selection face literally.

**Runtime (`domain:cli`'s half) — right.**
- `resolveProjectDatabaseUrl`: the `memory-driver` rung is replaced by a refusal that stands ahead of every rung (`namesRetiredMemoryEngine` reads the CONTRACT face, so the four spellings and `inmemory` are refused as the retirement, not as a typo). Pinned ahead of an explicit `file:` URL and of an env `memory://` URL, with a `sqlite`/`sqlite-wasm` control. The banner finding rides here: `resolveDevDatabase` passes `--fresh`'s file as `explicitUrl` and the refusal precedes it, so `os dev` prints no `Database:` row for a store the child would refuse (pinned in `dev-default-db.test.ts`).
- `resolveStandaloneDatabase`: `detectDriverFromUrl` now classifies `(memory|mingo)://` character-for-character as the CLI does, and `refuseRetiredMemoryEngine` refuses it naming the source (typed URL, `OS_DATABASE_URL`, or the declared DEFAULT datasource by name). `unsupportedDriverMessage` gives the engine's spellings the retirement sentence on both the env door and the zod `databaseDriver` config door. `StandaloneDatabaseDriverSchema` now enumerates the selection face, so the enum no longer offers a value its own doors refuse (the #21572 report's red pair in `standalone-stack.mysql.test.ts` is closed by that, not by a test rewrite). The `memory` arm leaves `createStandaloneStack`'s dispatch and `BootDriverKind` keeps the `never` check honest. Q2 a holds: every `bootSchemaStack` user and every embedder resolves through this seam; `probeMigrationTarget` catches and steps aside (`not_applicable`) so the boot owns the loud refusal, pinned in `sqlite-occupancy.test.ts`.
- Published surface, judged: narrowings — `ProjectDatabaseUrlSource` loses `'memory-driver'`; `ResolvedStandaloneDatabase.driver` narrows to exclude `memory`; `resolveProjectDatabaseUrl`, `resolveStandaloneDatabase`, `createStandaloneStack`, `createDefaultHostConfig` throw where they accepted. Widenings — two new exports from the package index, `namesRetiredMemoryEngine` and `retiredMemoryEngineMessage`, so the CLI's legacy resolver cannot word the retirement differently. Both halves are declared in the changeset. Right.
- The 5 runtime boots on `memory://` move to SQLite `:memory:` as ruled; `standalone-stack.test.ts` keeps a `memory://` case as a refusal pin and adds the `:memory:` round-trip as its control.

**CLI — right.**
- `inferDriverTypeFromUrl` throws `UnsupportedDriverError` (`recognized: false`) for both schemes rather than returning `''` (which would be the #3276 silent fall-through to SQLite) or a kind (which would leave the refusal to a message naming a variable the operator never set). `resolveStorageDefinition` refuses the spellings with the shared sentence and drops the `memory` definition arm. The storage-driver module header now says, measured, which boots reach it (legacy `os serve` only) — the observation the dev's first report flagged, discharged.
- The `--database-driver` allowlist and `--help` drop `memory` by derivation (`database-driver-allowlist.pin.test.ts` pins the parse-time refusal for all three spellings). `database-driver-flag.ts`'s "no driver is withheld today" doc is corrected. `dev`/`start` `--database` help offers `:memory:` instead of `memory://`.
- The parity pin (`driver-vocabulary-parity.test.ts`): no exemption. A derived row asserts the withdrawn set equals exactly the four `memory` spellings; refuse rows for the three spellings on both hosts in dev and prod naming both replacements; URL-door rows for `memory://`, `memory://named`, `mingo://`, `MINGO://upper` on both hosts; a `:memory:` control accepted as `sqlite` on both. The `mingo://` cross-host divergence (#21572 report, class b) is closed.
- `duplicates.null-seam.test.ts` moves to a seam double per Q2 a (`vi.hoisted` mock of `bootSchemaStack`, no boot on the engine), keeps the real command on the refusal path, asserts the probes reached the seam and the stack was shut down, and adds the answering-seam control. Both halves pinned.

**Docs, QA, ledger — right, with one nit.**
- Four docs pages advertise the retirement and the two replacements; `drivers.mdx` says plainly that a declared non-default `driver: 'memory'` datasource and direct construction still build, which keeps the claim as narrow as the enforcement. `content/docs/releases/**` untouched.
- Nit (wrong, non-blocking): `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx` line 522 ends "`memory://` and `mingo://` are refused — see the callout below", but the memory callout is the one inserted ABOVE "What it boots" (lines 505–517); the two callouts below it are about `os start` vs `os serve` and `os secret orphans`. One word, a docs-only follow-up or a rider on the next edit of the page.
- `cli.json`: `cli.dev-boot-contract` revision 4 turns the memory tier into a REFUSED variant with a negative naming where each spelling is refused, adds the `-d :memory:` variant, and corrects the source note; `cli.migrate-duplicates-inventory` revision 4 cites the seam-double pin and keeps the `memory://` run as a `boot_failed` probe; devx's rider `5967974683` rewrites the six live `this.error()` strings and leaves the two dated history entries, which is the right reading of a history ledger. Each bump carries its history entry.
- `scripts/driver-memory-census.ledger.json`: the CLI row's `why` no longer claims a boot spelling routes to the driver; axis unchanged.

**Not in the diff, as ruled:** `@objectstack/driver-memory` untouched; no `packages/spec` path beyond the declared row; no ADR touched. ADR grep for the surface: ADR-0115 names driver-memory in plugin-dev's zero-config assembly, which is a direct construction (`dev-plugin.ts` still does `new InMemoryDriver(...)`) and so outside the ruling's "boot spelling" — not contradicted; no `scripts/adr-anchors/` entry anchors any touched file.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/21492-retire-memory-boot-store.md`: `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/cli` at `minor`; title `fix(spec,runtime,cli)!:`; a `**BREAKING**` paragraph; a FROM → TO migration for each of the three doors (flag/env to `--fresh`, URL to `:memory:`, default datasource to a SQLite one); exactly one ADR-0087 marker, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, with the other categories closed on facts.

- The three packages that publish a change are exactly the three in the changeset; the files outside them (docs, QA, the census ledger) publish nothing.
- The level is right under this repo's narrowing kit: an accept-set narrowing is BREAKING and ships as `minor` under the launch-window convention (`check:changeset-no-major` green, and the same shape as `713b0fa76d` which the #21572 card names).
- The ADR-0087 marker is right: no authorable key, metadata body or stored shape moves — `datasource.driver: memory` still parses against `MemoryConfigSchema` — so there is nothing a conversion could rewrite, and a rewrite to a different engine would not be truthful. No `retiredKey()` tombstone is owed because no authorable key is removed. `Check Changeset` green on this head.
- The two added runtime exports are a widening inside a narrowing changeset; the dominant arm is the narrowing, the widening is declared in the body, and the Clause-② line carries one arm as the rule requires.

Clause-②: yes (narrowing) — right. The spec's published selection face drops three spellings and both hosts refuse boot selections they accepted; the PR body's line-initial `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` matches the changeset's.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev flags (report `5970391589`, PR Acceptance notes) and the seat's ACCEPT (`5970431837`), each answered:

1. **Scope question raised to triage — a declared NON-default `driver: 'memory'` datasource still builds through `service-datasource`'s factory.** Judged: the PR's refusal scope matches the rulings' text as the text was derived. `5967968291`'s sentence "a stored `datasource.driver: memory` parses and is refused at boot" descends from the #21572 report's `declared_datasource_door` reading, which is the DEFAULT-datasource door (`datasourceUrlOf` translating the declaration to `memory://` on the runtime's URL ladder); that door is refused here by name. The same ruling keeps `driver-memory` unretired and says a direct construction is not a boot spelling, and no ruling names a non-default declared datasource. The question is correctly escalated, not decided by the seat, and it does not block: the ruling's enumerated doors (flag, env, `memory://` / `mingo://` on both hosts, `os migrate`, programmatic `createStandaloneStack`, the default datasource) are all closed and pinned, the `service-datasource` door is `domain:services`, and the docs claim exactly what is enforced. Carrier: triage's answer on #21492; a follow-up card in `domain:services` only if triage rules the door in.
2. **The flag door refuses in oclif's wording, naming no replacement.** Answered: the ruling itself says the flag and `--help` drop the spelling by derivation and forbids consumer-side subtraction, so the parse-time refusal in oclif's words is the ruling's own consequence; the next door the operator reaches (env, URL, config) names both replacements. Right; noted in the PR, not filed.
3. **`os dev --database memory://x` prints the parent's `Database:` row before the serve child refuses.** Answered: the parent prints the URL it was handed and the child refuses that same URL, so one boot no longer names two stores; this is the shape every unsupported scheme has. The banner finding proper (a `file:` row beside an in-memory child) is refused before any row and pinned. Right.
4. **The CLI's `@objectstack/driver-memory` dependency kept.** Answered: dropping a published dependency is a packaging decision the ruling did not take; the ledger row says why it stays. Right.
5. **Merge commit `6727c656c6` with git's default message, no trailer pair.** Non-blocking: the landing squashes, so the merge commit's message does not reach `main`; the authored commits carry the model-free pair per AGENTS.md.
6. **devx rider: six live strings rewritten, two history entries kept.** Right — a history entry records what was true when written.
7. **QA `no_sql_seam` negative moved to the seam double, `memory://` run kept as a `boot_failed` probe.** Matches Q2 a verbatim.
8. `open_questions: []` on the final report; A1–A6 all measured and the ablation turned each host's own pins red and left the other green, which is the reverse verification the parity pin promises.

Observations, not blocking, none filed (carrier none):
- The dev SQLite step-down's last rung still constructs the engine (declared "Unchanged" in the changeset and named in `drivers.mdx`). It is not a spelling and the ruling does not reach it; it remains the one non-spelling path to a store that refuses tenant-scoped reads.
- `Console Pin Gate` is `skipped` on this head (path filter). No spec export is removed and no api-surface shard moves, so a pinned-sibling import cannot break on a removed symbol; the one removed union member (`ProjectDatabaseUrlSource.'memory-driver'`) is a backend runtime type. The landing seat still owes the sibling grep Post-Task step 4 names.
- `environment-variables.mdx`'s `OS_DATABASE_POOL_MAX` row still lists `memory` among pool-less drivers; still true on the contract face (a declared datasource), so not a defect.

Governance: not a governed-surface PR (no `docs/adr/**`, `.claude/**`, `skills/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/NORTH-STAR.md` in the file list; `Governed Surface Queue Guard` green). Same-repo head. 1,376 changed lines, under the 5,000 human-merge threshold. Security posture: the change removes a boot door to a store with no tenant isolation; no role, permission or policy surface moves.

**Gates on this head (latest run per name, read 2026-10-03T15:34Z after the last two concluded):** every one of the seven required contexts is `success` — `Lint & Repo Gates` (111228240772, concluded 15:33Z), `TypeScript Type Check` (111231304620), `Test Core` (111233671067; shards 1–6 all `success`, 1/6 concluded 15:33Z), `Dogfood Regression Gate` (111229963643; 1–3 all `success`), `Build Core` (111228304857), `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)` (111228304871), `Governed Surface Queue Guard` (111228240740). Also `success`: Build Docs, Check Changeset (111229651411), Check Documentation Links, Dogfood Verify CLI, Flag docs affected by code changes, Spec property liveness, the three claim/single-writer/part-of guards, the four Type Check sub-jobs. `skipped` (path-filtered, not a verdict): Auto Label, Check PR Size re-run (its first run 111228240696 was `success`), Console Pin Gate, Packed-tarball smoke. No run on this head is unfinished and none failed.
